_comment: §3.2.0: the defect classes that make the >=90% coverage claim falsifiable. Each names the tier CHECK that catches it; g-defect-class-coverage fails unless that check is covered by a verdict-flipping mutation (so the class is provably caught, not merely listed). `tier:"t3"` classes are reachable only by the semantic tier (WP-3b) and are excluded from Scope A's denominator, which is printed separately. Sources are the DC-NN defect classes named in §1.1 / §2.1.3 and the T2 check table (§3.2.3).

classes.describe: a stray label without hideLabel on a non-input container (label:"Card1" on the page shell)
a breakpoint styling key present in some but not all of desktop/tablet/mobile
a breakpoint value contradicting the base level for the same key
a fixed height on a page-shell card (dimensions.height wrapping the whole page)
two styling channels for one property (legacy fontSize/fontWeight alongside v7 desktop.font)
a stylingBox duplicated at both the base level and a breakpoint block
an action wired to an illegal (actionOwner, actionName) pair — the silent no-op button
a formSettings key illegal for the form kind (an active submit pipeline on a read-only list)
a referenceListId that is not {module, bare name} (a dotted name, or flat module/referenceListName keys)
an authorable:false component in the artifact (the banned columns component)
an unresolved $role token left as a literal colour value in compiler output
an entity property bound with the wrong casing so the cell renders blank (semantic; T3/WP-3b)
a container that clips its own content — the height:30px page-shell class, observable only in a rendered document
two siblings painted over each other at the target viewport
appearance asserted from an instrument that captures none — must degrade to partial, never pass (banned behaviour T15)
an action whose consequence is evidenced by a toast rather than a raw backend read
